items.explanation: I, me. は marks the topic ('as for me') and だ is the plain form of です ('is'). Japanese often leaves 私 out when it is clear who is speaking.
items.mnemonic: Wa-ta-shi: 'What a sheep? No, it's me!'

example.reading: わたしは がくせいだ。

items.explanation: You. の shows possession: あなたの本 is 'your book'. With people you know, Japanese prefers their name plus さん, because あなた can sound distant.
items.mnemonic: Ah, NA-ta: pointing at the person you are talking to.

example.reading: これは あなたの ほんだ。

items.explanation: Teacher. 先 (ahead) + 生 (life): someone who was born, or learned, before you. It is also a title for doctors and lawyers, added after the name. You never call yourself 先生.
items.mnemonic: The teacher sensei senses what you didn't study.

example.reading: たなかせんせいは にほんじんだ。

items.explanation: Student, especially a university student; school pupils are usually 生徒 (せいと). 学 means study.
items.mnemonic: Gaku-sei: a student says 'gak!' when the exam starts.

example.reading: あには だいがくの がくせいだ。
example.meaning: My older brother is a university student.

items.explanation: Friend; also written 友達. と means 'with' here.
items.mnemonic: Tomo-dachi: tomorrow I'll see my friend.

example.reading: ともだちと はなす。

items.explanation: Family. Counting people: 一人 (ひとり), 二人 (ふたり), then 三人 (さんにん), 四人 (よにん).
items.mnemonic: Ka-zoku: a car full of family on a trip to the zoo.

example.reading: わたしの かぞくは よにんだ。
example.meaning: There are four people in my family.

items.explanation: Child or children; Japanese nouns have no plural form. いる is used for people and animals that exist or are present.
items.mnemonic: Ko-domo: a child in a dome-shaped playground.

example.reading: こどもが さんにん いる。

items.explanation: Your own older brother, when talking to others. Someone else's older brother is お兄さん (おにいさん). Japanese has separate words for older and younger siblings: a younger brother is 弟 (おとうと).
items.mnemonic: Ani: 'Any problem? My big brother will help.'

example.reading: あには せんせいだ。
example.meaning: My older brother is a teacher.

items.explanation: Your own older sister, when talking to others; someone else's is お姉さん (おねえさん). A younger sister is 妹 (いもうと). に marks where someone is.
items.mnemonic: Ane: 'Ah, neh, my big sister knows everything.'

example.reading: あねは とうきょうに いる。
example.meaning: My older sister is in Tokyo.

items.explanation: Name. Asking politely: お名前は? ('your name?').
items.mnemonic: Na-ma-e: 'Nah, my name is not that!'

example.reading: わたしの なまえは アナだ。

items.culture_note: Japanese names are said family name first: in 山田太郎, 山田 is the family name.
